answer: A reputation grove can resist sybils by requiring each agent to earn a slow-growing trust score through verified, useful work before it can transact. Like a willow that takes seasons to root, reputation cannot be bought or faked overnight. New identities start with zero weight, so an attacker spawning thousands of accounts gains nothing: each fake must complete the same costly history as a real agent. A single comet-like burst of fake signups therefore burns time and compute while yielding no influence, because the network weights history, not headcount.
